issues.description: First branch still dereferences t.result.Load() without nil-check after the fix
issues.detail: The top of run() reads `output := t.result.Load()` and then does `closed(output.done)` and passes output around. If a previous leader panicked and set t.result back to nil, this very first Load can return nil and the existing `closed(output.done)` line will panic with exactly the nil-deref this patch claims to fix. The patch only hardened the CompareAndSwap-failure path; the symmetric path at line ~441 (the early `if output := t.result.Load(); output != nil` branch) needs the same guard, or the race is half-fixed.

issues.description: Returning a bare nil *result from run() will blow up every caller
issues.detail: `return nil // Leader panicked but we did see a result.` returns a nil *result up the stack. Every call site of run() that does output.Fatal, output.done, output.Value, etc. now has a brand-new nil-deref site one frame up. You haven't fixed the panic; you've moved it. If the legitimate behavior after a leader panic is `the query failed`, then synthesize a result with Fatal set (e.g. an ErrLeaderPanicked) and return that. A nil return on a function that everywhere else returns a non-nil *result is hostile to every caller and to the maintainer six months from now. Also: the comment says `but we did see a result` which is the opposite of what the code does.

issues.description: Shadowing the outer named return `output` inside the CAS-failure branch is a footgun
issues.detail: The enclosing function has `output *result` as a named return. Inside the CAS-failure branch the patch declares `output := t.result.Load()` with `:=`, shadowing it. That works today but the named return + shadow combo is exactly the pattern that gets miscompiled in someone's head during the next edit and silently returns the wrong thing. Use a different local name (`leader`, `winner`) or assign with `=`.

issues.description: Race window between CompareAndSwap failure and Load is not actually closed
issues.detail: Between `!t.result.CompareAndSwap(nil, output)` returning false and the subsequent `t.result.Load()`, the leader can complete-and-clear (per the panic-cleanup path described in the PR). So the new Load can still return nil even after CAS failed. That's handled here, fine. But the same logic applies to the first branch (issue 1) AND nothing documents the invariant `t.result may transition pending->nil under us` anywhere near the field declaration. If the invariant is real, document it on the atomic field; if it isn't, this whole fix is treating the symptom.

issues.description: Commit/PR description punts the actual cycle-detection question
issues.detail: `The current cycle detection only checks the immediate call path via the path linked list. So only on the branch where we immediately know that the caller may be a child (t.result.Load() != nil) we run the cycle check. A follow up PR will be added for dependency cycles.` This is the patch admitting that after the refactor, cycle detection is only invoked on one of the two paths that the original code reached, and that this is known-incomplete. That's a behavior change, not just a race fix. Either land the follow-up at the same time or call this out in the commit message as a deliberate narrowing of cycle detection with a TODO and a test that pins the new behavior.

issues.description: No test reproduces the nil-deref or the leader-panic recovery
issues.detail: A race-condition fix with no regression test is a fix that will regress. The PR body describes a precise sequence (leader panics, sets t.result to nil, waiters Load it, deref) which is exactly the shape of a test: synchronize a fake task to panic mid-leadership, fire N waiters at it, assert no panic and a sensible error. Without that test, the next refactor reintroduces the bug and nobody knows.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: refactor + race fix + cycle-detection scope change in one diff
issues.detail: This is doing three things: (1) extract checkCycle into its own method, (2) fix the nil-deref on the CAS-failure path, (3) implicitly narrow when cycle detection runs. Each is reviewable on its own. The refactor is fine and obvious; the race fix needs the test from issue 6; the cycle-detection narrowing needs the follow-up PR referenced. Splitting would have made (2) trivially landable today.

`// Leader panicked but we did see a result.` should presumably be `did NOT see a result` (the code is in the nil branch). Small thing, but it's the comment that explains the load-bearing weird return-nil, so it needs to be right.

issues.description: checkCycle extraction is GOOD-TASTE, keep it
issues.detail: The extracted method drops a level of indentation, removes the `cycle != nil` post-check (now a plain return), and makes the call site one line. This is the part of the patch that's obviously right. Mention it only because the rest of the patch needs work and I don't want this piece thrown out with the bathwater.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The refactor to extract checkCycle is good taste and should stay. The race fix is half-done: the patch hardens the CompareAndSwap-failure path against t.result going nil, but the symmetric early branch (`if output := t.result.Load(); output != nil`) still does `closed(output.done)` and can panic on the exact same race the PR describes. Worse, the new `return nil` on leader-panic gives every caller of run() a fresh nil-deref site one frame up and is mis-commented to boot; synthesize a result with Fatal set instead. The PR also admits it narrows when cycle detection runs and defers the rest to a follow-up, which is a behavior change that needs a test pinning the new behavior. No regression test for the leader-panic race. Split into three patches, add the test, fix the symmetric path, and stop returning bare nil.
